description: Whether an actor may put a thing on, into which slot, and what wearing it comes to (US-1 and US-4 of `124-items-equipment-economy`). Each case carries the whole input — the catalogue rows it names, the WORLD’s own slot table, the actor’s held levels, every stack they have anywhere and the fully resolved ItemTuning — so a harness in any language reproduces it with no defaults table, no world file and no KB. Two things here are not reproducible by a port that compiled its slots: `back` is a slot declared by content and worn by an actor, and `ring` holds two because the world said two. `expected.facts` is every stack said in the 110 vocabulary, which is where the one-model claim is legible — an equipped stack emits `has_equipped/3` AND `has_item/3`, because `carried_weight/2` sums the latter and a worn breastplate is still steel you are carrying. Refusals are evaluated in EQUIP_REFUSALS order — unknown, not_held, no_slot, unknown_slot, already_equipped, slot_full, requires — and `forbidden` NEVER appears: permissibility is `forbids/4`’s and a pure function may not call a KB, so a corpus that pinned one would be pinning a guess. Regenerate with `npm run items-corpus`.

cases.name: a-sword-into-the-slot-the-world-declared
cases.note: The plain case, and the one every other is a refusal of: the item names a slot, the world declares it, the actor is carrying it and nothing is in it yet. The action atom is the world’s own `equipAction`, which is what a host charges and a norm gates.

cases.name: a-cloak-into-a-slot-no-engine-was-compiled-with
cases.note: THE case authored slots exist for. `back` is not in any `EquipmentSlot` union — it is a row of `WorldIR.items.slots` — and a port that compiled its slots reproduces nothing here. Adding it needed no code change in any of the four engines.

cases.name: a-second-ring-into-a-slot-that-holds-two
cases.note: The pack’s own justifying example for `equip_slot_capacity/2`, from the open side: one ring on and room for another, because the world said two. Capacity is reported whether or not it refuses, so a paper doll can draw the empty socket.

cases.name: a-third-ring-refused-by-the-world’s-own-capacity
cases.note: Two rings, not five. The refusal is the world’s number and not core’s: the same case under a world that authored `capacity: 3` is available, which is why the whole slot table rides in the input.

cases.name: an-item-the-catalogue-never-declared
cases.note: An absence rather than a verdict: no slot, no capacity, no requirement read, and the id reported back so a host can say which item it could not find. A port that resolves a missing row to "not equipment" reports the wrong rung.

cases.name: what-nobody-is-carrying-cannot-be-worn
cases.note: `can_equip/2` requires `has_item(A, I, _)` before anything else about the item is read — you cannot put on what is not in your hands. Refused before the slot is even looked up, which is why the ladder’s order is part of the contract.

cases.name: a-loaf-is-not-equipment
cases.note: An item that authored no `equip_slot/2` at all. Distinct from `unknown_slot` on purpose: this is content that is right and simply not wearable, and a host says so differently.

cases.name: an-item-naming-a-slot-this-world-does-not-declare
cases.note: Authored content that is WRONG — a torc for a slot no world row declares. Core refuses rather than inventing the slot, because a slot invented at runtime is a slot no `equip_slot_capacity/2` bounds.

cases.name: what-is-already-worn-is-not-worn-again
cases.note: Held and equipped at once, which is the normal state of a worn item: `has_equipped/3` and `has_item/3` are both true of a breastplate on a back. The refusal reads the second fact, not the absence of the first.

cases.name: plate-that-wants-a-skill-this-actor-has-not-learned
cases.note: An `item_requires/3` the actor is one level short of. The unmet requirement is REPORTED rather than counted, so a host says "you need Heavy Armour 2" instead of "you cannot wear this" — the same discipline the skill module’s refusals follow.

cases.name: the-same-plate-once-the-skill-is-there
cases.note: The identical input with one level added — nothing about the item, the slot or the world changed. A port whose requirement check is an inequality in the wrong direction passes the case above and fails this one.

cases.name: a-worn-breastplate-still-weighs-thirty
cases.note: The identity claim, in facts. One stack in one place, said with `has_equipped/3` AND `has_item/3`, because `carried_weight/2` sums `has_item/3` — if wearing the plate retracted it, 30 units of steel would weigh nothing the moment it went on and `encumbered/1` would stop meaning anything. Here it means the actor is over the world’s 40. The same ledger also holds a cuirass in a chest and two loaves in the mud, said with `container_contains/3` and `item_at/3`, and neither weighs anything on anybody — four places, one representation, one sum that knows which of them is a body.
